profile.headline: Software Engineer | React, TypeScript, Python, Node | Ex-Paramount | Clients include Apple, NBC
profile.summary:
I'm a senior software engineer and team lead with a focus on design systems, accessibility, and high-stakes user-facing products.



At Parchment (an Instructure company), I lead the Tasty design system — an a11y-first component library used across multiple product teams, built to WCAG and 508 standards before the 2025 federal mandate made it a priority industry-wide. I was promoted to senior within a year and stepped into the team lead role shortly after, where I've focused on mentorship, adoption, and making sure acquired companies can interoperate without losing a contract.


Before Parchment: interactive election maps and social card systems for NBC's elections team, the iPhone 11 launch onsite at Apple, and frontend leadership for enterprise clients at Paramount.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Shipped a full-stack digital pathology app (React/Fabric.js/OpenSeadragon, C# backend) that
pathologists prefer over the industry-standard Aperio ImageScope

Implemented human-in-the-loop ML workflow enabling pathologists to annotate whole-slide
images, trigger automated analysis, and provide corrective feedback for model retraining

Architected coordinate transformation layer bridging declarative React patterns with imperative
canvas APIs for sub-pixel annotation accuracy on gigapixel medical images

Refactored annotation state to Zustand and built a tool-factory abstraction, establishing clean
state boundaries and reusable patterns across a complex canvas UI

Reduced loading time for dashboard pages and slide viewer by over 3 seconds

Ensured application architecture and logging practices met HIPAA compliance requirements
for protected health information (PHI)

Worked across the full stack, including backend API design and familiarity with FHIR/HL7 data
formats as well as third-party authentication MFA flow integration

projects.title: Diffuse
projects.description:
CLI/Github Actions tool that uses AST analysis to surface potentially risky changes to git commits and assigns an overall risk score to the PR, with configurable values.

These risky changes include function changes without test changes, param updates, return type changes, and more.

It isn't meant to replace code review, but to shine a light on areas that could use extra scrutiny, especially when multiple teams may be using a specific function or component, and changes could have downstream effects in another repo somewhere else that aren't visible to the developer.

projects.title: Spotify Exporter
projects.description: I built a script to fetch and export track data from my spotify playlists. Then I saw a reddit thread asking about an app to do the same thing, and turned my script into a full app so users can export track data from public playlists and albums, and log in with Spotify to export private playlists and albums. From the one reddit comment I made, I get about 90 visitors per week
